Please note that any changes targeting the original code should remove the line number, colon, and leading space. 1: # Superpoint & Multi-Scale Geometric Filtering Pipeline for Speleological Point Clouds 2: 3: ## 1. Overview & Problem Statement 4: 5: Speleological 3D point clouds acquired via Terrestrial Laser Scanning (TLS) and mobile SLAM LiDAR frequently capture both the subterranean **cavern interior** (bedrock walls, vaulted ceilings, floors, stalactites, stalagmites, breakdown boulders) and **exterior non-cavern clutter** near cave entrances, dolines, and skylights (trees, bushes, hanging roots, surface terrain outside the drip line, and anthropogenic scanner artifacts). 6: 7: When uncleaned point clouds are fed into the repository's reconstruction and skeletonization pipeline ([src/pipeline_main.cpp](file:///home/projval/Documents/cgal/src/pipeline_main.cpp)): 8: 1. **Screened Poisson Reconstruction (`PoissonRecon`)** attempts to fit watertight isosurfaces around high-entropy foliage and exterior talus slopes, ballooning octree complexity and distorting entrance topology. 9: 2. **Mean Curvature Flow Skeletonization (`skeleton_extraction`)** generates spurious topological branches extending into tree canopies and exterior terrain. 10: 11: This document records the **architectural review, empirical dataset audit, engineering decisions, and step-by-step implementation specification** for filtering non-cavern geometry using **Superpoint Transformer (SPT) $\ell_0$-cut pursuit partitioning** combined with **CloudCompare-compatible multi-scale geometric and enclosure descriptors**. 12: 13: --- 14: 15: ## 2. Empirical Audit of the Remote Dataset & Hardware Constraints 16: 17: ### 2.1 Remote S3 Dataset Audit (`http://150.164.212.12:8010/`) 18: 19: The remote S3 Sync Manager (`bucket: ufmg-vale-esp-artefatos`, `region: us-east-2`) hosts **38 point clouds** under `point-clouds/` and **47 meshes** under `meshes/`. Inspecting the `.ply` headers of all 38 remote point clouds (alongside local raw scans in [input/](file:///home/projval/Documents/cgal/input)) reveals two distinct cohorts: 20: 21: | Cohort | Scans | Representative Examples | Existing PLY Schema | Audit Findings | 22: | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- | :--- | 23: | **A. European / Alpine Karst** | 16 | `archamps_*`, `baume_de_longeaigue`, `cascade_de_motiers`, `cocaliere_cotepatiere`, `encanaux_*`, `event_de_peyrejal`, `faux_monnayeurs`, `grotte_de_la_*`, `hoelloch_*` (3), `lauiloch`, `les_cavottes`, `markov_spodmol`, `rupt_du_puits`, `vallorbe`, `vers_chez_le_brandt` | `x, y, z`, `red, green, blue`, `nx, ny, nz`, `scalar_Intensity`, `scalar_Classification`, `scalar_Illuminance_(PCV)` (± `scalar_Synthetic_Flag`) | • Normals and `PCV` (ShadeVis ambient occlusion) are precomputed.
• 13 of 16 are stored as uncompressed **ASCII PLY** (up to 1.18 GB).
• Several files are segments of the same cave system (`hoelloch_*`, `archamps_*`, `encanaux_*`). | 24: | **B. Brazilian Caves (Iron Formation, Quartzite, Karst)** | 22 | `arco_do_andre`, `BR_0034`, `casa_de_pedra`, `CAV04`, `gruta_do_janelao`, `lapa_boi`, `lapa_da_onça`, `lapa_dos_anjos`, `lapa_dos_desenhos`, `lapa_dos_troncos`, `lapa_jean_louis`, `lapinha`, `mina_de_fabrica`, `N5S_0021_0027`, `S11A_0257`, `S11D_0001`, `S11D_0061`, `diaclise` | Heterogeneous: many contain **only `x, y, z`** (`lapa_da_onça`, `lapa_dos_troncos`, `lapinha`) or `x, y, z, r, g, b` (`arco_do_andre`, `lapa_dos_anjos`, `S11A_0257`). | • **Missing normals (`nx, ny, nz`)**, **missing `PCV`**, and **missing `scalar_Classification`** across nearly all scans.
• Many clouds are pre-decimated to $\le 10\text{M}$ vertices on S3.
• 12 of the 38 S3 clouds lack `scalar_Intensity` entirely. | 25: 26: ### 2.2 Why Existing `scalar_Classification` and `meshes/` Cannot Be Used as Ground Truth 27: 28: 1. **`scalar_Classification` is Ground-vs-Non-Ground, Not Cavern-vs-Vegetation:** 29: Statistical inspection of [input/BaumeDeLongeaigue.ply](file:///home/projval/Documents/cgal/input/BaumeDeLongeaigue.ply) and [input/rupt.ply](file:///home/projval/Documents/cgal/input/rupt.ply) confirmed that `scalar_Classification` contains only binary values (`1.0` and `2.0`) corresponding to standard ASPRS LiDAR ground filtering (e.g., CSF): 30: * In [input/rupt.ply](file:///home/projval/Documents/cgal/input/rupt.ply), `Class 1.0` ($150,821$ pts) has $z_{\text{mean}} = +2.44\text{ m}$ and $n_z = -0.362$ (downward-pointing **cave ceiling**), whereas `Class 2.0` ($196,133$ pts) has $z_{\text{mean}} = -2.37\text{ m}$ and $n_z = +0.282$ (upward-pointing **cave floor**). 31: * Trusting `scalar_Classification` as a `Cavern vs. Remove` label would train a model to strip cave ceilings or floors. 32: 2. **Remote `meshes/` Were Generated Directly from Uncleaned Clouds:** 33: The 47 meshes in `meshes/` on the S3 server were reconstructed directly from the raw/unfiltered point clouds without manual vegetation removal and therefore cannot be used as distance-based ground-truth masks. 34: 35: ### 2.3 Local Hardware Profile 36: 37: All development, feature extraction, and superpoint partitioning target the local workstation first: 38: * **GPU:** NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4050 Laptop GPU (**6,141 MiB VRAM**, ~5.0 GB usable alongside display server) 39: * **CPU:** 13th Gen Intel Core i7-13650HX (**20 logical threads**) 40: * **System RAM:** **31 GiB DDR5** (+ 8 GiB Swap) 41: * **CUDA Environment:** CUDA 12.8 (Driver 570.172.08) 42: 43: --- 44: 45: ## 3. Architectural Decisions Record (ADR) 46: 47: | Decision ID | Topic | Decision | Rationale | 48: | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | 49: | **ADR-01** | **Implementation Strategy (Option 2 Selected)** | Build a **standalone Python + C++ prototyping pipeline** that exports multi-scalar diagnostic `.ply` files for CloudCompare first; defer native C++/CUDA integration into `preprocess_core` until validated. | Rapidly validates feature separability, $\ell_0$-cut pursuit regularization, and graph filtering thresholds via visual inspection in CloudCompare before committing to low-level C++/CUDA kernel refactoring. | 50: | **ADR-02** | **Unsupervised Superpoint Filtering Prior to Supervised SPT** | Replace immediate supervised Transformer training (DALES transfer learning, 4-class Lovász-Softmax) with **unsupervised/physical superpoint graph filtering** driven by CloudCompare-style geometric and enclosure descriptors. | Because trusted semantic labels do not exist across the 38 S3 clouds, supervised neural network fine-tuning cannot be executed directly. However, SPT's non-parametric $\ell_0$-cut pursuit + superpoint graph rules require zero labels and can later generate pseudo-labels if supervised training is desired. | 51: | **ADR-03** | **Global Subsampling & Global Features Before Spatial Tiling** | Reverse Step 1 of the initial draft: run **global $3\text{ cm}–4\text{ cm}$ subsampling**, **global normal orientation (WNNC)**, and **global upward enclosure** on the full cloud *before* any spatial tiling. | Slicing a cave into $40\text{ m} \times 40\text{ m}$ tiles before computing ambient occlusion or upward raycasting detaches high cavern ceilings from floors near tile boundaries, creating false "open-sky" artifacts inside deep chambers. | 52: | **ADR-04** | **Mandatory `float64` Centroid Subtraction** | Always compute and subtract the cloud centroid in `float64` (`pos_f64 - mean_f64`) before casting coordinates to `float32`. | Scans in projected national grids (e.g., Swiss LV95 $X \approx 2.53 \times 10^6\text{ m}$ in `BaumeDeLongeaigue.ply`) suffer a **$0.25\text{ m}$ `float32` quantization step (ULP)**, which destroys $3\text{ cm}$ voxelization and local covariance eigenvalues if cast prior to centering. | 53: | **ADR-05** | **Trajectory-Free Normal Orientation via WNNC** | Use **Winding Number Normal Consistency (WNNC)** ([src/wnnc](file:///home/projval/Documents/cgal/src/wnnc)) instead of sensor-trajectory orientation. | None of the 38 S3 clouds have trajectory files, and 35 of 38 lack `Gps_Time`. WNNC globally orients normals consistently inward/outward without trajectories. | 54: | **ADR-06** | **Purely Geometric + Enclosure Feature Bank (Drop `Intensity` & `RGB`)** | Exclude `scalar_Intensity`, `RGB`, and raw elevation $z$ from the classification logic; rely exclusively on translation-invariant multi-scale geometry and 3D roof enclosure. | 12 of 38 S3 clouds lack `Intensity`, and some clouds (`rupt.ply`) contain synthetic grayscale duplicated across `R=G=B`. Pure geometry + enclosure works identically on minimal `(x, y, z)` clouds (`lapa_da_onça`, `lapa_dos_troncos`, `lapinha`). | 55: 56: --- 57: 58: ## 4. End-to-End Pipeline Architecture (Option 2) 59: 60: ```mermaid 61: flowchart TD 62: A["S3 / Local Input Cloud (.ply)"] --> B["Stage 1: Float64 Centering &\nGlobal 3-4cm Grid Subsampling"] 63: B --> C["Stage 2: Global Normal Orientation\n(CUDA WNNC / Coherent Inward Normals)"] 64: C --> D["Stage 3: Multi-Scale P0 Feature Extraction\n(Fine r=0.15m, Coarse r=0.50m + Upward Cone Occlusion)"] 65: D --> E["Stage 4: l0-Cut Pursuit Partition\n(P0 Voxels -> P1 Fine Superpoints -> P2 Coarse Superpoints)"] 66: E --> F["Stage 5: Superpoint Graph Scoring\n& Geodesic / Roof-Enclosure Filtering"] 67: F --> G["Stage 6A: Diagnostic Multi-Scalar .ply\n(Inspectable in CloudCompare)"] 68: F --> H["Stage 6B: Cleaned Cavern .ply\n(Ready for PoissonRecon & Skeletonization)"] 69: ``` 70: 71: ### Stage 1: Ingestion, `float64` Coordinate Centering & Global $P_0$ Subsampling 72: 1. Parse ASCII or binary little-endian `.ply` from S3 (`https://ufmg-vale-esp-artefatos.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/point-clouds/`) or local `input/`. 73: 2. Store the original `float64` centroid $\boldsymbol{\mu} = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N \mathbf{p}_i$ in metadata so exported clouds can be restored to their original coordinate system. 74: 3. Translate points: $\tilde{\mathbf{p}}_i = \text{float32}(\mathbf{p}_i - \boldsymbol{\mu})$. 75: 4. Apply a $P_0$ voxel grid subsample at **$d_0 = 0.03\text{ m}$ to $0.04\text{ m}$** (using either the repository's [`CudaDecimator`](file:///home/projval/Documents/cgal/src/preprocess/src/cuda_decimator.cu) or fast 64-bit spatial voxel hashing in Python/C++). For a 10M-point S3 cloud, this produces **$1.5\text{M}–3.5\text{M}$ evenly spaced points**, homogenizing TLS/SLAM density gradients and bounding RAM usage well within 31 GB. 76: 77: ### Stage 2: Global Normal Orientation (WNNC) 78: 1. If the input cloud lacks reliable oriented normals, run the repository's CUDA-accelerated **WNNC** solver ([src/wnnc](file:///home/projval/Documents/cgal/src/wnnc)) on the subsampled cloud. 79: 2. Enforce consistent **inward-pointing cavern convention** (or outward convention verified via signed winding number gradient): 80: * **Cavern Ceiling:** normal points **downward** ($n_z < -0.25$). 81: * **Cavern Floor & Exterior Ground:** normal points **upward** ($n_z > +0.25$). 82: * **Cavern Walls & Tree Trunks:** normal is horizontal ($|n_z| \approx 0$). 83: 84: ### Stage 3: Multi-Scale CloudCompare & SPT Feature Bank ($P_0$) 85: For each subsampled point $p_i$, compute the local $3 \times 3$ covariance matrix over spherical neighborhoods at **two spatial scales** ($r_{\text{fine}} = 0.15\text{ m}$ to capture leaves/twigs, and $r_{\text{coarse}} = 0.50\text{ m}$ to capture rock sheets vs. bush canopies), yielding ordered eigenvalues $\lambda_1 \ge \lambda_2 \ge \lambda_3 \ge 0$ and eigenvectors $\mathbf{v}_1, \mathbf{v}_2, \mathbf{v}_3$: 86: 87: #### A. Local Eigen-Descriptors & Normal Statistics (Computed at $r_{\text{fine}}$ and $r_{\text{coarse}}$) 88: * **Verticality:** 89: $$V = 1 - |n_z| \in [0, 1]$$ 90: * **Horizontality & Signed Horizontality:** 91: $$H = |n_z| \in [0, 1], \quad H_{\text{signed}} = n_z \in [-1, 1]$$ 92: *(Crucial cue: $n_z < -0.25$ uniquely identifies overhanging bedrock and cavern ceilings, which never occur on exterior ground).* 93: * **Rugosity / Surface Variation (CloudCompare Curvature):** 94: $$\kappa = \frac{\lambda_3}{\lambda_1 + \lambda_2 + \lambda_3} \in \left[0, \frac{1}{3}\right]$$ 95: *(Cavern rock sheets have $\kappa_{\text{coarse}} < 0.06$; foliage and bushes approach isotropic 3D scattering $\kappa \in [0.15, 0.33]$).* 96: * **Planarity, Linearity, and Scattering (Sphericity):** 97: $$P = \frac{\lambda_2 - \lambda_3}{\lambda_1}, \quad L = \frac{\lambda_1 - \lambda_2}{\lambda_1}, \quad S = \frac{\lambda_3}{\lambda_1}$$ 98: * **Normal Dispersion / Roughness Entropy:** 99: $$D_{\mathbf{n}} = 1 - \left\| \frac{1}{|\mathcal{N}_r(i)|} \sum_{j \in \mathcal{N}_r(i)} \mathbf{n}_j \right\|_2 \in [0, 1]$$ 100: *(Even fractured or scalloped cave walls maintain coherent normal orientations at $r = 0.20\text{ m}$ ($D_{\mathbf{n}} < 0.18$), whereas foliage exhibits chaotic normals ($D_{\mathbf{n}} > 0.45$)).* 101: 102: #### B. ## 6. Empirical Benchmarks & Massive-Scale Optimizations (Up to 311.7M Points)

The standalone pipeline is implemented in [spt_filter.py](file:///home/projval/Documents/cgal/spt_filter.py) backed by C++20 OpenMP/Eigen3/WNNC kernels in [src/spt_filter/spt_kernels.cpp](file:///home/projval/Documents/cgal/src/spt_filter/spt_kernels.cpp) (`build/libspt_kernels.so`).

### Key Algorithmic & Scaling Refinements
1. **Always-On Global WNNC Normal Estimation & Physical Raycast Verification:**
   - Pre-existing `.ply` normals in Cohort A (`BaumeDeLongeaigue.ply`, `diaclase.ply`) are frequently unoriented or outward-pointing, which previously inverted `signed_horizontality` ($n_z$) and scrambled Floor vs. Ceiling separation.
   - Stage 2A now unconditionally executes the **Winding Number Normal Consistency (WNNC)** solver ([`spt_compute_wnnc_normals`](file:///home/projval/Documents/cgal/src/spt_filter/spt_kernels.cpp#L1133-L1290)) over a 60,000-point carrier cloud ($40\text{ iterations}$, $O(N \log N)$ Barnes-Hut octree treecode) and propagates inward-oriented normals to all $P_0$ voxels.
   - Stage 2B blends the global WNNC orientation with local PCA eigenvectors proportionally to surface planarity while computing sign-invariant structure tensor dispersion ($D_{\mathbf{n}}$) on unsmoothed local PCA directions (expanding sparse neighborhood searches up to $3r$ so low-density cave vaults never trigger high-entropy fallbacks).
   - Stage 3 ([`spt_compute_enclosure`](file:///home/projval/Documents/cgal/src/spt_filter/spt_kernels.cpp#L606-L790)) verifies physical normal polarity along $\pm Z$ using **rock-coherent occlusion**: points with a coherent rock ceiling above ($O_{\text{roof}} > O_{\text{down,rock}} + 0.12$) are enforced to point upward ($n_z > 0$, **Floor**), while points with a rock floor below and no rock ceiling above ($O_{\text{down,rock}} > O_{\text{roof}} + 0.12$) are enforced to point downward ($n_z < 0$, **Ceiling**)—even when tall trees grow on the hillside above the cave.
2. **Explicit Floor / Wall / Ceiling Structural Zone Separation (`scalar_cave_zone`):**
   - Stage 4 incorporates strongly weighted `signed_horizontality` ($1.2 \times n_z$) and vertical occlusion differential ($0.8 \times (O_{\text{roof}} - O_{\text{down}})$) into the $\ell_0$-cut pursuit feature vector so $P_1$ superpoints never merge floors, walls, and ceilings across cave conduits.
   - Stage 5 classifies every Cavern superpoint into explicit structural zones exported to `scalar_cave_zone`: `0 = Floor` ($n_z \ge +0.35$), `1 = Wall` ($|n_z| < 0.35$), `2 = Ceiling` ($n_z \le -0.35$), alongside `3 = Vegetation` and `4 = Exterior Ground`.
3. **2D-Manifold-Gated Cone Raycasting (`roof_occlusion` vs. `upward_occlusion`):**
   - In tropical forest caves (`Lp_JL.ply`, `point-clouds_S11A_0257.ply`, `Lp_Boi.ply`), 15–25m tall trees outside and above the entrance cause lower canopy branches and exterior ground to experience high raw upward ray hits ($O_{\text{up}} \in [0.56, 0.97]$).
   - Weighting occupancy cells by coarse-scale 2D rock coherence ($P_{\text{coarse}} > 0.32, D_{\mathbf{n},\text{coarse}} < 0.35, \kappa_{\text{coarse}} < 0.12, S_{\text{coarse}} < 0.25$) ensures porous 3D leaf canopies contribute `0.000–0.004` to `roof_occlusion`, while true bedrock ceilings yield high `roof_occlusion`.
4. **Positive-Evidence Canopy Detection & Topological Connected-Component Filtering (0% False Positives on Interior Caves):**
   - Replaced catch-all negative scoring with positive-evidence multi-scale 3D foliage criteria (requiring simultaneous fine-scale and coarse-scale volumetric scattering, rugosity, and normal dispersion under open sky $O_{\text{roof}} < 0.15$).
   - Scaled feature radii proportionally to voxel size ($r_{\text{fine,eff}} = \max(r_{\text{fine}}, 3.75\,d_0)$, $r_{\text{coarse,eff}} = \max(r_{\text{coarse}}, 10.0\,d_0)$) to prevent discrete voxel-lattice staircasing on $8\text{ cm}–12\text{ cm}$ grids.
   - Implemented **Step 5 Topological Superpoint Graph Connected-Component Filtering**: candidate exterior vegetation superpoints are clustered in 3D space and validated only if the connected component has macroscopic size ($\ge 500$ $P_0$ voxels, $\ge 300$ canopy voxels) **and** extends into open exterior space ($> 4.5\text{ m}$ from any enclosed cave vault seed). Rough wall pockets or stalactite clusters inside pure interior caves (`rupt`, `BaumeDeLongeaigue`, `diaclase`, `interior_lapinha`) stay within $\le 4.07\text{ m}$ of the cave vault and are 100% retained as `Cavern`.
5. **Out-of-Core Chunked Streaming for 100M–300M+ Point Clouds:**
   - `stream_subsample_ply` and `stream_export_cleaned_ply` stream 15M-vertex chunks from disk and map $P_0$ predictions and WNNC-oriented normals back to full resolution via `spt_map_points_to_p0`, keeping peak memory under **3.5 GB RAM**.

## Part 1: Why Your Superpoints Group Multiple Classes (And How to Fix It)

In your current Stage 3–5 implementation (`spt_kernels.cpp`), four interacting mechanisms cause $P_1$ superpoints to merge cave rock with exterior vegetation and misclassify lower canopy structures as `Wall`:

### 1. Dynamic Radius Inflation on $8\text{ cm}–12\text{ cm}$ Voxel Grids Blurs Boundaries

* **What is happening:** To process 108M–311M point clouds like `Lp_JL.ply` and `Lp_Boi.ply`, Stage 6 increases the $P_0$ voxel size $d_0$ to $8\text{ cm}–12\text{ cm}$ and scales the feature radii to $r_{\text{fine,eff}} = \max(r_{\text{fine}}, 3.75\,d_0)$ ($30\text{ cm}–45\text{ cm}$) and $r_{\text{coarse,eff}} = \max(r_{\text{coarse}}, 10.0\,d_0)$ ($80\text{ cm}–120\text{ cm}$). When a $1.2\text{ m}$ sphere straddles a cave entrance wall and an overhanging bush, the covariance matrix averages both geometries together. Because the features transition smoothly across that $1.2\text{ m}$ band, $\ell_0$-cut pursuit sees no sharp gradient and merges the rock and bush into a single $P_1$ superpoint.


* **The Fix:** **Decouple the partition features from the classification features.** Use only **fine-scale, unsmoothed features** ($r_{\text{part}} = 2.5\,d_0$ to $3.0\,d_0$, or $k=16$ nearest neighbors) inside the Stage 4 $\ell_0$-cut pursuit vector $\mathbf{f}_i$. Reserve the $10.0\,d_0$ coarse features exclusively for Stage 5 superpoint scoring (computed *after* partitioning, or aggregated only over points belonging to the same fine superpoint).

### 2. Heavy Weighting of Smoothed $n_z$ (`1.2 * n_z`) in Cut-Pursuit

* **What is happening:** Stage 2B blends global WNNC normals with local PCA eigenvectors, and Stage 4 injects `1.2 * n_z` and `0.8 * (O_roof - O_down)` into the cut-pursuit feature vector. Near a cave entrance or sinkhole rim, both a vertical rock face and a vertical tree trunk or steep talus slope have $\vert{}n_z\vert{} \approx 0$ and $O_{\text{roof}} \approx 0$. Because `1.2 * n_z` dominates the Euclidean feature distance in cut-pursuit, the partitioner happily merges vertical trunks and entrance bushes directly into the adjacent cave wall. Worse, Stage 5 assigns any non-canopy superpoint with $\vert{}n_z\vert{} < 0.35$ to `1 = Wall`, which is why the lower forest and entrance slope turn bright green in your screenshot.


* **The Fix:**
1. Reduce the weight of $n_z$ in Stage 4 cut-pursuit from `1.2` to `0.35`, and increase the weight of **unsmoothed fine normal dispersion ($D_{\mathbf{n},\text{fine}}$)** and **fine scattering ($S_{\text{fine}}$)** to `1.5`.
2. In Stage 5, **never allow `Wall` (`|n_z| < 0.35`) to act as a default fallback when $O_{\text{roof}}$ is low**. A vertical surface with $O_{\text{roof}} < 0.20$ located outside the drip line is either a **Tree Trunk** ($L_{\text{fine}} > 0.45$ or small horizontal cross-section) or **Exterior Cliff / Talus**—not an interior cave wall.





### 3. Unbounded $k=10$ k-NN Adjacency & High `pcp_cutoff = [10, 30]`

* **What is happening:** Stage 4 builds a $k=10$ nearest-neighbor graph and runs cut-pursuit with `pcp_regularization = [0.04, 0.15]` and minimum segment size `pcp_cutoff = [10, 30]`. On a $12\text{ cm}$ voxel grid, `pcp_cutoff = 10` forces every $P_1$ superpoint to contain at least 10 voxels ($\sim 1.5\text{ m}$ span), absorbing small shrubs or roots touching the rock. Meanwhile, a pure $k$-NN graph without a maximum edge length bridges across empty air gaps between sparse foliage and the cliff face.


* **The Fix:**
1. **Prune Long Graph Edges:** In your $k=10$ adjacency graph builder, drop any edge $(i, j)$ where $\Vert{}\mathbf{p}_i - \mathbf{p}_j\Vert{}_2 > 3.5\,d_0$ (unless a node would become completely isolated, in which case keep only its single nearest neighbor). This physically severs air bridges between overhanging branches and bedrock.
2. **Add Contrast-Sensitive Edge Weights:** Instead of uniform spatial edge weights, weight every graph edge $(i, j)$ by normal and scattering similarity:

$$w_{ij} = \frac{1}{\Vert{}\mathbf{p}_i - \mathbf{p}_j\Vert{}_2 + \epsilon} \cdot \exp\left(-\frac{1 - \vert{}\mathbf{n}_i \cdot \mathbf{n}_j\vert{}}{\sigma_n^2}\right) \cdot \exp\left(-\frac{(D_{\mathbf{n},i} - D_{\mathbf{n},j})^2}{\sigma_D^2}\right)$$



When cut-pursuit pays nearly zero penalty to cut across a sharp normal or roughness jump, superpoints snap cleanly to the rock-foliage interface.
3. **Force Over-Segmentation at $P_1$:** Lower `pcp_cutoff` from `[10, 30]` to **`[3, 15]`** and `pcp_regularization` from `[0.04, 0.15]` to **`[0.015, 0.08]`**. Splitting a cave wall into 30% more superpoints is completely harmless, whereas merging two classes into one $P_1$ superpoint is unrecoverable.

Right now, your Stage 5 rules try to force a hard decision (`0` to `4`) on *every* superpoint, which causes the uncertain entrance zone to collapse into green `Wall` predictions. For training a neural network or graph classifier, **you only need labels where your physical heuristics are 99% certain**, and you can mask out the rest:

844:         f"-> N_P1={num_p1:,} -> N_P2={num_p2:,} (edges={num_edges:,})"

948: # -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
949: def run_cutmix_stress_test(
950:     lib: ctypes.CDLL,
951:     xyz_f64: np.ndarray,
952:     normals_in: Optional[np.ndarray],
953:     voxel_size: float = 0.04,
954: ) -> None:
955:     """
956:     Grafts synthetic 3D trees (cylindrical trunks + high-entropy leaf canopies) and
957:     exterior terrain outside the entrance of the cave, plus a complex internal speleothem
958:     cluster deep inside the cave, and evaluates P1 Oracle mIoU and Classification IoU.
959:     """
960:     rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
961:     min_pt = xyz_f64.min(axis=0)
962:     max_pt = xyz_f64.max(axis=0)
963: 
964:     # Place entrance exterior zone just beyond max Y of the conduit
965:     ext_y0 = max_pt[1] + 0.5
966:     ground_z = np.percentile(xyz_f64[:, 2], 35)
967: 
968:     # 1. Synthetic Exterior Ground Slope (Class 2: 15,000 pts)
969:     n_ground = 15000
970:     gx = rng.uniform(min_pt[0], max_pt[0], n_ground)
971:     gy = rng.uniform(ext_y0, ext_y0 + 14.0, n_ground)
972:     gz = ground_z + 0.08 * (gy - ext_y0) + rng.normal(0.0, 0.025, n_ground)
973:     ground_xyz = np.column_stack([gx, gy, gz])
974:     ground_normals = np.column_stack([
975:         rng.normal(0.0, 0.05, n_ground),
976:         rng.normal(-0.08, 0.05, n_ground),
977:         np.ones(n_ground),
978:     ]).astype(np.float32)
979:     ground_normals /= np.linalg.norm(ground_normals, axis=1, keepdims=True)
980: 
981:     # 2. Synthetic 3D Trees: Trunks + Fractal/Volumetric Foliage Canopies (Class 1: 25,000 pts)
982:     tree_xyz_list = []
983:     tree_norm_list = []
984:     tree_centers = [
985:         (min_pt[0] + 4.0, ext_y0 + 2.5),
986:         (min_pt[0] + 10.0, ext_y0 + 4.0),
987:         (min_pt[0] + 16.0, ext_y0 + 3.0),
988:         (min_pt[0] + 7.0, ext_y0 + 8.5),
989:         (min_pt[0] + 14.0, ext_y0 + 9.0),
990:     ]
991:     for tx, ty in tree_centers:
992:         base_z = ground_z + 0.08 * (ty - ext_y0)
993:         # Trunk points (vertical cylinder r=0.22m, height=4.5m)
994:         n_trunk = 1000
995:         theta = rng.uniform(0, 2 * np.pi, n_trunk)
996:         tz = rng.uniform(base_z, base_z + 4.5, n_trunk)
997:         rad = 0.22 + rng.normal(0, 0.015, n_trunk)
998:         t_pts = np.column_stack([tx + rad * np.cos(theta), ty + rad * np.sin(theta), tz])
999:         t_nrm = np.column_stack([np.cos(theta), np.sin(theta), rng.normal(0, 0.1, n_trunk)]).astype(np.float32)
1000:         t_nrm /= np.linalg.norm(t_nrm, axis=1, keepdims=True)
1001:         tree_xyz_list.append(t_pts)
1002:         tree_norm_list.append(t_nrm)
1003: 
1004:         # Canopy leaf clusters (high scattering & chaotic normals, radius ~ 2.8m)
1005:         n_canopy = 4000
1006:         c_pts = []
1007:         for _ in range(8):
1008:             sub_c = np.array([
1009:                 tx + rng.uniform(-1.8, 1.8),
1010:                 ty + rng.uniform(-1.8, 1.8),
1011:                 base_z + rng.uniform(3.5, 7.5),
1012:             ])
1013:             c_pts.append(sub_c + rng.normal(0.0, 0.65, (n_canopy // 8, 3)))
1014:         c_pts = np.vstack(c_pts)
1015:         c_nrm = rng.normal(0.0, 1.0, c_pts.shape).astype(np.float32)
1016:         c_nrm /= np.linalg.norm(c_nrm, axis=1, keepdims=True)
1017:         tree_xyz_list.append(c_pts)
1018:         tree_norm_list.append(c_nrm)
1019: 
1020:     veg_xyz = np.vstack(tree_xyz_list)
1021:     veg_normals = np.vstack(tree_norm_list)

1023:     # Combine Original Cave (Class 0) + Synthetic Vegetation (Class 1) + Exterior Ground (Class 2)
1024:     comb_xyz = np.vstack([xyz_f64, veg_xyz, ground_xyz])

1026:         np.zeros(len(xyz_f64), dtype=np.int32),

1051:     union_oracle = np.sum((oracle_p0_bin == 1) | (p0_gt_bin == 1))
1052:     oracle_cavern_iou = 100.0 * inter_oracle / max(union_oracle, 1)
1053:

1058:     fn = int(np.sum((pred_bin == 0) & (p0_gt_bin == 1)))
1059:     tn = int(np.sum((pred_bin == 0) & (p0_gt_bin == 0)))
1060: 
1061:     precision = 100.0 * tp / max(tp + fp, 1)
1062:     recall = 100.0 * tp / max(tp + fn, 1)
1063:     cavern_iou = 100.0 * tp / max(tp + fp + fn, 1)
1064:     remove_iou = 100.0 * tn / max(tn + fp + fn, 1)
1065: 
1066:     print(f"  P1 Superpoint Oracle Cavern IoU : {oracle_cavern_iou:.2f}% (Target >= 96.0%)")
1067:     print(f"  Unsupervised Filter Precision   : {precision:.2f}%")
1068:     print(f"  Unsupervised Filter Recall      : {recall:.2f}%")
1069:     print(f"  Unsupervised Filter Cavern IoU  : {cavern_iou:.2f}%")
1070:     print(f"  Unsupervised Filter Remove IoU  : {remove_iou:.2f}%")

486:         ctypes.c_float(0.04),
487:         ctypes.c_int32(180000),
488:         p0_normals.ctypes.data_as(f32_p),
489:     )
490:     t_wnnc = time.perf_counter()
491: 
492:     # --- Stage 2B & 3A: Multi-Scale Geometric Eigenvalues & Local PCA Normal Alignment ---
493:     # Ensure fine and coarse radii are at least 3.75x and 10.0x voxel_size so larger P0 grids
494:     # (e.g. 0.08m or 0.12m on 100M-300M scans) never suffer discrete voxel-lattice staircasing.
495:     r_fine_eff = max(r_fine, voxel_size * 3.75)
496:     r_coarse_eff = max(r_coarse, voxel_size * 10.0)
497:     occ_cell_eff = max(0.20, voxel_size * 4.0)
498: 
499:     fine_feats = np.empty((num_p0, 6), dtype=np.float32)
500:     coarse_feats = np.empty((num_p0, 6), dtype=np.float32)
501: 
502:     lib.spt_compute_scale_features(
503:         p0_xyz.ctypes.data_as(f32_p),
504:         p0_normals.ctypes.data_as(f32_p),
505:         ctypes.c_int32(num_p0),
506:         ctypes.c_float(r_fine_eff),
507:         ctypes.c_int32(1),
508:         fine_feats.ctypes.data_as(f32_p),
509:     )
510: 
511:     lib.spt_compute_scale_features(
512:         p0_xyz.ctypes.data_as(f32_p),
513:         p0_normals.ctypes.data_as(f32_p),
514:         ctypes.c_int32(num_p0),
515:         ctypes.c_float(r_coarse_eff),
516:         ctypes.c_int32(0),
517:         coarse_feats.ctypes.data_as(f32_p),
518:     )
519:     t2 = time.perf_counter()
520: 
521:     # --- Stage 3B: Global 3D Cone Enclosure Raycasting & Floor/Ceiling Normal Verification ---
522:     enclosure_feats = np.empty((num_p0, 4), dtype=np.float32)
523:     lib.spt_compute_enclosure(
524:         p0_xyz.ctypes.data_as(f32_p),
525:         p0_normals.ctypes.data_as(f32_p),
526:         fine_feats.ctypes.data_as(f32_p),
527:         coarse_feats.ctypes.data_as(f32_p),
528:         ctypes.c_int32(num_p0),
529:         ctypes.c_float(occ_cell_eff),
530:         ctypes.c_float(45.0),
531:         enclosure_feats.ctypes.data_as(f32_p),
532:     )
533:     upward_occlusion = enclosure_feats[:, 0]
534:     roof_occlusion = enclosure_feats[:, 1]
535:     downward_occlusion = enclosure_feats[:, 2]
536:     cavern_enclosure = enclosure_feats[:, 3]
537: 
538:     # Compute signed_horizontality (nz), horizontality (|nz|), and verticality (1 - |nz|)
539:     # AFTER WNNC + physical vertical raycast verification (Floor: nz > 0, Ceiling: nz < 0)
540:     signed_horizontality = p0_normals[:, 2].copy()
541:     horizontality = np.abs(signed_horizontality)
542:     verticality = 1.0 - horizontality
543:     vert_asymmetry = roof_occlusion - downward_occlusion
544:     t3 = time.perf_counter()
545: 
546:     # --- Stage 4: Hierarchical l0-Cut Pursuit Superpoint Partitioning (P0 -> P1 -> P2) ---
547:     # Weight signed_horizontality (1.2) and vertical occlusion asymmetry (0.8) strongly
548:     # so Floor (nz > 0, up_occ > down_occ), Wall (|nz| ~ 0), and Ceiling (nz < 0, down_occ > up_occ)
549:     # are strictly separated into distinct superpoints.
550:     part_feats = np.column_stack([
551:         fine_feats[:, 1],             # planarity_fine [0, 1]
552:         fine_feats[:, 2],             # scattering_fine [0, 1]
553:         fine_feats[:, 3],             # linearity_fine [0, 1]
554:         coarse_feats[:, 0] * 3.0,     # rugosity_coarse scaled to [0, 1]
555:         verticality,                  # verticality [0, 1]
556:         signed_horizontality * 1.2,   # signed_horizontality [-1.2, +1.2]
557:         vert_asymmetry * 0.8,         # upward - downward occlusion [-0.8, +0.8]
558:         fine_feats[:, 5],             # normal_dispersion_fine [0, 1]
559:         cavern_enclosure * 0.8,       # 3D cavern enclosure [0, 0.8]
560:     ]).astype(np.float32)
561:     part_feats = np.ascontiguousarray(part_feats, dtype=np.float32)
562: 
563:     p1_labels = np.empty(num_p0, dtype=np.int32)
564:     num_p1 = lib.spt_partition_superpoints(
565:         p0_xyz.ctypes.data_as(f32_p),
566:         part_feats.ctypes.data_as(f32_p),
567:         ctypes.c_int32(num_p0),
568:         ctypes.c_int32(part_feats.shape[1]),
569:         ctypes.c_float(max(voxel_size * 4.5, 0.18)),
570:         ctypes.c_float(p1_reg),
571:         ctypes.c_float(0.02),
572:         ctypes.c_int32(p1_cutoff),
573:         p1_labels.ctypes.data_as(i32_p),
574:     )
575: 
576:     p2_labels = np.empty(num_p0, dtype=np.int32)
577:     num_p2 = lib.spt_partition_superpoints(
578:         p0_xyz.ctypes.data_as(f32_p),
579:         part_feats.ctypes.data_as(f32_p),
580:         ctypes.c_int32(num_p0),
581:         ctypes.c_int32(part_feats.shape[1]),
582:         ctypes.c_float(max(voxel_size * 7.5, 0.30)),
583:         ctypes.c_float(p2_reg),
584:         ctypes.c_float(0.008),
585:         ctypes.c_int32(p2_cutoff),
586:         p2_labels.ctypes.data_as(i32_p),
587:     )
588: 
589:     # Build P1 Superpoint Boundary Adjacency Graph
590:     max_edges = num_p1 * 30 + 10000
591:     edge_u = np.empty(max_edges, dtype=np.int32)
592:     edge_v = np.empty(max_edges, dtype=np.int32)
593:     num_edges = lib.spt_build_superpoint_graph(
594:         p0_xyz.ctypes.data_as(f32_p),
595:         p1_labels.ctypes.data_as(i32_p),
596:         ctypes.c_int32(num_p0),
597:         ctypes.c_int32(num_p1),
598:         ctypes.c_float(max(voxel_size * 6.0, 0.25)),
599:         ctypes.c_int32(max_edges),
600:         edge_u.ctypes.data_as(i32_p),
601:         edge_v.ctypes.data_as(i32_p),
602:     )
603:     edge_u = edge_u[:num_edges]
604:     edge_v = edge_v[:num_edges]
605:     t4 = time.perf_counter()
606: 
607:     # --- Stage 5: Superpoint Graph Scoring & Topological Geodesic Filtering ---
608:     sp_counts = np.bincount(p1_labels, minlength=num_p1).astype(np.float32)
609:     sp_inv = 1.0 / np.maximum(sp_counts, 1.0)
610: 
611:     def sp_mean(arr: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
612:         return np.bincount(p1_labels, weights=arr, minlength=num_p1).astype(np.float32) * sp_inv
613: 
614:     sp_pos = np.column_stack([sp_mean(p0_xyz[:, d]) for d in range(3)])
615:     sp_nz = sp_mean(signed_horizontality)
616:     sp_vert = sp_mean(verticality)
617:     sp_rug_fine = sp_mean(fine_feats[:, 0])
618:     sp_plan_fine = sp_mean(fine_feats[:, 1])
619:     sp_scat_fine = sp_mean(fine_feats[:, 2])
620:     sp_lin_fine = sp_mean(fine_feats[:, 3])
621:     sp_ndisp_fine = sp_mean(fine_feats[:, 5])
622: 
623:     sp_rug_coarse = sp_mean(coarse_feats[:, 0])
624:     sp_plan_coarse = sp_mean(coarse_feats[:, 1])
625:     sp_scat_coarse = sp_mean(coarse_feats[:, 2])
626:     sp_ndisp_coarse = sp_mean(coarse_feats[:, 5])
627: 
628:     sp_up_occ = sp_mean(upward_occlusion)
629:     sp_roof_occ = sp_mean(roof_occlusion)
630:     sp_down_occ = sp_mean(downward_occlusion)
631:     sp_enclosure = sp_mean(cavern_enclosure)
632: 
633:     # 1. Unary Vegetation / High-Entropy Clutter Score [0, 1]
634:     entropy_score = np.clip(
635:         0.30 * (sp_rug_coarse / 0.13)
636:         + 0.25 * (sp_scat_coarse / 0.30)
637:         + 0.25 * (sp_ndisp_fine / 0.38)
638:         + 0.20 * (sp_scat_fine / 0.28),
639:         0.0,
640:         1.5,
641:     )
642:     open_sky_factor = (
643:         np.clip(1.0 - (sp_roof_occ / 0.22), 0.0, 1.0)
644:         * np.clip(1.0 - (sp_enclosure / 0.35), 0.0, 1.0)
645:     )
646:     # 2D planar surfaces (smooth rock walls/floors/ceilings) cannot have high vegetation score
647:     non_planar_factor = np.clip(1.0 - (np.maximum(sp_plan_fine, sp_plan_coarse) - 0.34) * 3.0, 0.0, 1.0)
648:     unary_veg_score = np.clip(entropy_score * open_sky_factor * non_planar_factor, 0.0, 1.0)
649: 
650:     # 2. Fast Multi-Source Geodesic Distance on Superpoint Graph (Virtual Source Dijkstra)
651:     def multisource_dijkstra(seeds: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
652:         if len(seeds) == 0 or num_edges == 0:
653:             return np.full(num_p1, 999.0, dtype=np.float32)
654:         virtual_src = num_p1
655:         u_all = np.concatenate([edge_u, edge_v, np.full(len(seeds), virtual_src, dtype=np.int32), seeds])
656:         v_all = np.concatenate([edge_v, edge_u, seeds, np.full(len(seeds), virtual_src, dtype=np.int32)])
657:         w_all = np.concatenate([edge_dist, edge_dist, np.zeros(2 * len(seeds), dtype=np.float32)])
658:         mat = sparse.csr_matrix((w_all, (u_all, v_all)), shape=(num_p1 + 1, num_p1 + 1))
659:         dists = csgraph.dijkstra(mat, directed=False, indices=virtual_src)[:num_p1]
660:         return np.minimum(dists, 999.0).astype(np.float32)
661: 
662:     if num_edges > 0:
663:         edge_dist = np.linalg.norm(sp_pos[edge_u] - sp_pos[edge_v], axis=1).astype(np.float32)
664:     else:
665:         edge_dist = np.empty(0, dtype=np.float32)
666: 
667:     # Confirmed Cavern Vault Seeds: enclosed coherent rock ceilings, walls, shafts, or floors
668:     vault_seeds = np.where(
669:         (sp_counts >= max(6, p1_cutoff // 3))
670:         & (sp_rug_fine < 0.12)
671:         & (sp_ndisp_fine < 0.34)
672:         & ((sp_plan_fine > 0.34) | (sp_plan_coarse > 0.34))
673:         & (
674:             (sp_enclosure > 0.28)
675:             | (sp_roof_occ > 0.24)
676:             | ((sp_nz < -0.22) & (sp_down_occ > 0.22))
677:         )
678:     )[0]
679:     dist_to_vault_graph = multisource_dijkstra(vault_seeds) if len(vault_seeds) > 0 else np.zeros(num_p1, dtype=np.float32)
680:     if len(vault_seeds) > 0:
681:         vault_tree = cKDTree(sp_pos[vault_seeds])
682:         dist_to_vault_euclid, _ = vault_tree.query(sp_pos, k=1)
683:         dist_to_vault = np.minimum(dist_to_vault_graph, dist_to_vault_euclid.astype(np.float32))
684:     else:
685:         dist_to_vault = np.zeros(num_p1, dtype=np.float32)
686: 
687:     # Candidate Open-Sky Vegetation Canopy Superpoints:
688:     # Note: A true cave ceiling overhang must be a coherent 2D rock surface (high planarity, low scattering/dispersion).
689:     # Without this check, downward-facing WNNC normals on tree canopies above ground would look like overhangs!
690:     is_ceiling_overhang = (
691:         (sp_nz < -0.20)
692:         & (sp_down_occ > 0.18)
693:         & (sp_plan_fine > 0.35)
694:         & (sp_ndisp_fine < 0.32)
695:     )
696:     raw_canopy_mask = (
697:         (~is_ceiling_overhang)
698:         & (sp_roof_occ < 0.15)
699:         & (sp_enclosure < 0.22)
700:         & (dist_to_vault > 1.8)
701:         & (sp_plan_fine < 0.34)
702:         & (sp_rug_fine > 0.10)
703:         & (sp_scat_fine > 0.20)
704:         & (sp_ndisp_fine > 0.32)
705:         & (sp_plan_coarse < 0.34)
706:         & ((sp_rug_coarse > 0.13) | (sp_scat_coarse > 0.28))
707:         & (sp_ndisp_coarse > 0.38)
708:     )
709: 
710:     # Candidate exterior trunk / branch / bush superpoints (unenclosed by rock roof, non-planar)
711:     raw_veg_support_mask = (
712:         raw_canopy_mask
713:         | (
714:             (~is_ceiling_overhang)
715:             & (sp_roof_occ < 0.16)
716:             & (sp_enclosure < 0.22)
717:             & (dist_to_vault > 1.8)
718:             & (
719:                 ((sp_plan_coarse < 0.35) & ((sp_lin_fine > 0.28) | ((sp_vert > 0.65) & (sp_ndisp_coarse > 0.45))))
720:                 | ((sp_plan_fine < 0.33) & (sp_ndisp_fine > 0.32) & (sp_rug_fine > 0.09))
721:             )
722:         )
723:     )
724: 
725:     # Topological Superpoint Graph Connected-Component Filtering (Step 5 of SPT Guide):
726:     # Connect candidate exterior vegetation superpoints within 3.5m (bridging gaps between adjacent branches)
727:     # and require both macroscopic cluster size (>= 500 P0 voxels, >= 300 canopy P0 voxels) AND that the
728:     # connected component actually extends into open exterior space (> 4.5m from any enclosed cave vault).
729:     # Any pocket inside a conduit whose component stays within <= 4.5m of the cave vault is reassigned to Cavern.
730:     validated_canopy_mask = np.zeros(num_p1, dtype=bool)
731:     cand_indices = np.where(raw_veg_support_mask)[0]
732:     if np.any(raw_canopy_mask) and len(cand_indices) > 0:
733:         cand_tree = cKDTree(sp_pos[cand_indices])
734:         pairs = cand_tree.query_pairs(r=3.5, output_type="ndarray")
735:         if len(pairs) > 0:
736:             u_c = cand_indices[pairs[:, 0]]
737:             v_c = cand_indices[pairs[:, 1]]
738:             sub_adj = sparse.csr_matrix(
739:                 (np.ones(2 * len(u_c), dtype=np.int32), (np.concatenate([u_c, v_c]), np.concatenate([v_c, u_c]))),
740:                 shape=(num_p1, num_p1),
741:             )
742:             n_comp, comp_labels = csgraph.connected_components(sub_adj, directed=False)
743:         else:
744:             n_comp = num_p1
745:             comp_labels = np.arange(num_p1, dtype=np.int32)
746:         comp_p0_sizes = np.bincount(comp_labels, weights=sp_counts * raw_veg_support_mask, minlength=n_comp)
747:         comp_canopy_p0 = np.bincount(comp_labels, weights=sp_counts * raw_canopy_mask, minlength=n_comp)
748:         comp_max_vault_dist = np.zeros(n_comp, dtype=np.float32)
749:         np.maximum.at(comp_max_vault_dist, comp_labels[cand_indices], dist_to_vault[cand_indices])
750:         valid_comps = (comp_p0_sizes >= 500) & (comp_canopy_p0 >= 300) & (comp_max_vault_dist > 4.5)
751:         validated_canopy_mask = raw_canopy_mask & valid_comps[comp_labels]
752: 
753:     canopy_seeds = np.where(validated_canopy_mask)[0]
754:     if len(canopy_seeds) > 0:
755:         dist_to_canopy_graph = multisource_dijkstra(canopy_seeds)
756:         canopy_tree = cKDTree(sp_pos[canopy_seeds])
757:         dist_to_canopy_euclid, _ = canopy_tree.query(sp_pos, k=1)
758:         dist_to_canopy = np.minimum(dist_to_canopy_graph, dist_to_canopy_euclid.astype(np.float32))
759:     else:
760:         dist_to_canopy = np.full(num_p1, 999.0, dtype=np.float32)
761: 
762:     # Tree Trunk & Branch Absorption: cylindrical/linear/foliage unenclosed superpoints attached to validated canopy seeds
763:     trunk_absorbed = (
764:         (len(canopy_seeds) > 0)
765:         & (~is_ceiling_overhang)
766:         & (dist_to_canopy < 5.0)
767:         & (dist_to_vault > 1.8)
768:         & (sp_roof_occ < 0.16)
769:         & (sp_enclosure < 0.22)
770:         & (
771:             ((sp_plan_coarse < 0.35) & ((sp_lin_fine > 0.26) | ((sp_vert > 0.65) & (sp_ndisp_coarse > 0.45))))
772:             | ((sp_plan_fine < 0.33) & (sp_ndisp_fine > 0.32) & (sp_rug_fine > 0.09))
773:             | ((dist_to_canopy < 3.5) & (sp_counts < p1_cutoff))
774:         )
775:     )
776: 
777:     # Exterior Ground Rule: unenclosed upward-facing single-layer horizontal surface outside the drip line
778:     # adjacent to validated exterior vegetation (note: sp_up_occ can be non-zero under trees, so gate on sp_roof_occ!)
779:     exterior_ground = (
780:         (len(canopy_seeds) > 0)
781:         & (dist_to_canopy < 15.0)
782:         & (dist_to_vault > 1.8)
783:         & (sp_nz > 0.45)
784:         & (sp_roof_occ < 0.12)
785:         & (sp_enclosure < 0.18)
786:         & (sp_down_occ < 0.10)
787:     )
788: 
789:     # Speleothem & Enclosed Cavern Protection (gated on ROCK roof/floor occlusion sp_roof_occ / sp_down_occ)
790:     speleothem_protected = (
791:         (sp_roof_occ > 0.22)
792:         | (sp_enclosure > 0.28)
793:         | is_ceiling_overhang
794:         | ((dist_to_vault < 10.0) & ((sp_roof_occ > 0.20) | (sp_down_occ > 0.20)) & (sp_ndisp_fine < 0.32))
795:     )
796: 
797:     # Continuous Superpoint Cavern Score [0, 1]
798:     sp_cavern_score = np.clip(
799:         0.80 + 0.20 * sp_enclosure - 0.65 * unary_veg_score * (dist_to_canopy < 8.0),
800:         0.0,
801:         1.0,
802:     )
803:     sp_cavern_score[speleothem_protected] = np.maximum(sp_cavern_score[speleothem_protected], 0.85)
804:     sp_cavern_score[validated_canopy_mask] = np.minimum(sp_cavern_score[validated_canopy_mask], 0.08)
805:     sp_cavern_score[trunk_absorbed] = np.minimum(sp_cavern_score[trunk_absorbed], 0.14)
806:     sp_cavern_score[exterior_ground] = np.minimum(sp_cavern_score[exterior_ground], 0.18)
807: 
808:     # Final Superpoint Semantic Class (Positive-Evidence Rule — Zero Hallucinated Vegetation):
809:     #   0 = Cavern (Floor, Wall, Ceiling, Speleothems)
810:     #   1 = Vegetation / Exterior Canopy & Trunks
811:     #   2 = Exterior Terrain / Unenclosed Ground outside Drip Line
812:     sp_pred_class = np.zeros(num_p1, dtype=np.int32)
813:     is_veg_sp = (validated_canopy_mask | trunk_absorbed) & (~speleothem_protected)
814:     is_ext_ground_sp = exterior_ground & (~is_veg_sp) & (~speleothem_protected)
815:     sp_pred_class[is_veg_sp] = 1
816:     sp_pred_class[is_ext_ground_sp] = 2
817: 
818:     # Structural Cave Zone Classification (Floor vs. Wall vs. Ceiling):
819:     #   0 = Cave Floor     (upward-facing nz > 0.30, or nz > 0.12 with ceiling above)
820:     #   1 = Cave Wall      (vertical rock surface |nz| <= 0.30)
821:     #   2 = Cave Ceiling   (downward-facing nz < -0.25, or nz < -0.10 with floor below)
822:     #   3 = Vegetation     (Class 1)
823:     #   4 = ExteriorGround (Class 2)
824:     sp_cave_zone = np.ones(num_p1, dtype=np.int32)  # Default Cavern zone = 1 (Wall)
825:     is_floor_sp = (sp_pred_class == 0) & (
826:         (sp_nz > 0.30) | ((sp_nz > 0.12) & (sp_roof_occ > sp_down_occ + 0.15))
827:     )
828:     is_ceiling_sp = (sp_pred_class == 0) & (~is_floor_sp) & (
829:         (sp_nz < -0.25) | ((sp_nz < -0.10) & (sp_down_occ > sp_roof_occ + 0.15))
830:     )
831:     sp_cave_zone[is_floor_sp] = 0
832:     sp_cave_zone[is_ceiling_sp] = 2
833:     sp_cave_zone[sp_pred_class == 1] = 3
834:     sp_cave_zone[sp_pred_class == 2] = 4
835: 
836:     t5 = time.perf_counter()
837: 
838:     # Map P1 superpoint predictions to P0 voxels
839:     p0_cavern_score = sp_cavern_score[p1_labels].astype(np.float32)
840:     p0_pred_class = sp_pred_class[p1_labels].astype(np.int32)
841:     p0_cave_zone = sp_cave_zone[p1_labels].astype(np.int32)
842: 
843:     print(
844:         f"[SPT Pipeline] N_orig={n_orig:,} -> N_P0={num_p0:,} ({voxel_size*100:.1f}cm) "
845:         f"-> N_P1={num_p1:,} -> N_P2={num_p2:,} (edges={num_edges:,})"
846:     )
847:     print(
848:         f"[Timing] Stage1(Subsample): {t_stage1:.2f}s | Stage2A(WNNC): {t_wnnc-t1:.2f}s | "
849:         f"Stage2B(MultiScale): {t2-t_wnnc:.2f}s | Stage3(Enclosure): {t3-t2:.2f}s | "
850:         f"Stage4(l0-CutPursuit): {t4-t3:.2f}s | Stage5(GraphFilter): {t5-t4:.2f}s | "
851:         f"Total: {t_stage1 + (t5-t1):.2f}s"
852:     )
853: 
854:     return {
855:         "centroid_f64": centroid_f64,
856:         "p0_to_orig": p0_to_orig,
857:         "orig_to_p0": orig_to_p0,
858:         "p0_xyz_f64": p0_xyz.astype(np.float64) + centroid_f64,
859:         "p0_xyz_centered": p0_xyz,
860:         "p0_normals": p0_normals,
861:         "verticality": verticality,
862:         "horizontality": horizontality,
863:         "signed_horizontality": signed_horizontality,
864:         "rugosity_fine": fine_feats[:, 0],
865:         "planarity_fine": fine_feats[:, 1],
866:         "scattering_fine": fine_feats[:, 2],
867:         "linearity_fine": fine_feats[:, 3],
868:         "omnivariance_fine": fine_feats[:, 4],
869:         "normal_dispersion_fine": fine_feats[:, 5],
