Overview & Problem Statement 4: 5: Speleological 3D point clouds acquired via Terrestrial Laser Scanning (TLS) and mobile SLAM LiDAR frequently capture both the subterranean **cavern interior** (bedrock walls, vaulted ceilings, floors, stalactites, stalagmites, breakdown boulders) and **exterior non-cavern clutter** near cave entrances, dolines, and skylights (trees, bushes, hanging roots, surface terrain outside the drip line, and anthropogenic scanner artifacts). 6: 7: When uncleaned point clouds are fed into the repository's reconstruction and skeletonization pipeline ([src/pipeline_main.cpp](file:///home/projval/Documents/cgal/src/pipeline_main.cpp)): 8: 1. **Screened Poisson Reconstruction (`PoissonRecon`)** attempts to fit watertight isosurfaces around high-entropy foliage and exterior talus slopes, ballooning octree complexity and distorting entrance topology. 9: 2. **Mean Curvature Flow Skeletonization (`skeleton_extraction`)** generates spurious topological branches extending into tree canopies and exterior terrain. 10: 11: This document records the **architectural review, empirical dataset audit, engineering decisions, and step-by-step implementation specification** for filtering non-cavern geometry using **Superpoint Transformer (SPT) $\ell_0$-cut pursuit partitioning** combined with **CloudCompare-compatible multi-scale geometric and enclosure descriptors**. 12: 13: --- 14: 15: ## 2. Empirical Audit of the Remote Dataset & Hardware Constraints 16: 17: ### 2.1 Remote S3 Dataset Audit (`http://150.164.212.12:8010/`) 18: 19: The remote S3 Sync Manager (`bucket: ufmg-vale-esp-artefatos`, `region: us-east-2`) hosts **38 point clouds** under `point-clouds/` and **47 meshes** under `meshes/`. Inspecting the `.ply` headers of all 38 remote point clouds (alongside local raw scans in [input/](file:///home/projval/Documents/cgal/input)) reveals two distinct cohorts: 20: 21: | Cohort | Scans | Representative Examples | Existing PLY Schema | Audit Findings | 22: | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- | :--- | 23: | **A. European / Alpine Karst** | 16 | `archamps_*`, `baume_de_longeaigue`, `cascade_de_motiers`, `cocaliere_cotepatiere`, `encanaux_*`, `event_de_peyrejal`, `faux_monnayeurs`, `grotte_de_la_*`, `hoelloch_*` (3), `lauiloch`, `les_cavottes`, `markov_spodmol`, `rupt_du_puits`, `vallorbe`, `vers_chez_le_brandt` | `x, y, z`, `red, green, blue`, `nx, ny, nz`, `scalar_Intensity`, `scalar_Classification`, `scalar_Illuminance_(PCV)` (± `scalar_Synthetic_Flag`) | • Normals and `PCV` (ShadeVis ambient occlusion) are precomputed.
• 13 of 16 are stored as uncompressed **ASCII PLY** (up to 1.18 GB).
• Several files are segments of the same cave system (`hoelloch_*`, `archamps_*`, `encanaux_*`). | 24: | **B. Brazilian Caves (Iron Formation, Quartzite, Karst)** | 22 | `arco_do_andre`, `BR_0034`, `casa_de_pedra`, `CAV04`, `gruta_do_janelao`, `lapa_boi`, `lapa_da_onça`, `lapa_dos_anjos`, `lapa_dos_desenhos`, `lapa_dos_troncos`, `lapa_jean_louis`, `lapinha`, `mina_de_fabrica`, `N5S_0021_0027`, `S11A_0257`, `S11D_0001`, `S11D_0061`, `diaclise` | Heterogeneous: many contain **only `x, y, z`** (`lapa_da_onça`, `lapa_dos_troncos`, `lapinha`) or `x, y, z, r, g, b` (`arco_do_andre`, `lapa_dos_anjos`, `S11A_0257`). | • **Missing normals (`nx, ny, nz`)**, **missing `PCV`**, and **missing `scalar_Classification`** across nearly all scans.
• Many clouds are pre-decimated to $\le 10\text{M}$ vertices on S3.
• 12 of the 38 S3 clouds lack `scalar_Intensity` entirely. | 25: 26: ### 2.2 Why Existing `scalar_Classification` and `meshes/` Cannot Be Used as Ground Truth 27: 28: 1. **`scalar_Classification` is Ground-vs-Non-Ground, Not Cavern-vs-Vegetation:** 29: Statistical inspection of [input/BaumeDeLongeaigue.ply](file:///home/projval/Documents/cgal/input/BaumeDeLongeaigue.ply) and [input/rupt.ply](file:///home/projval/Documents/cgal/input/rupt.ply) confirmed that `scalar_Classification` contains only binary values (`1.0` and `2.0`) corresponding to standard ASPRS LiDAR ground filtering (e.g., CSF): 30: * In [input/rupt.ply](file:///home/projval/Documents/cgal/input/rupt.ply), `Class 1.0` ($150,821$ pts) has $z_{\text{mean}} = +2.44\text{ m}$ and $n_z = -0.362$ (downward-pointing **cave ceiling**), whereas `Class 2.0` ($196,133$ pts) has $z_{\text{mean}} = -2.37\text{ m}$ and $n_z = +0.282$ (upward-pointing **cave floor**). 31: * Trusting `scalar_Classification` as a `Cavern vs. Remove` label would train a model to strip cave ceilings or floors. 32: 2. **Remote `meshes/` Were Generated Directly from Uncleaned Clouds:** 33: The 47 meshes in `meshes/` on the S3 server were reconstructed directly from the raw/unfiltered point clouds without manual vegetation removal and therefore cannot be used as distance-based ground-truth masks. 34: 35: ### 2.3 Local Hardware Profile 36: 37: All development, feature extraction, and superpoint partitioning target the local workstation first: 38: * **GPU:** NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4050 Laptop GPU (**6,141 MiB VRAM**, ~5.0 GB usable alongside display server) 39: * **CPU:** 13th Gen Intel Core i7-13650HX (**20 logical threads**) 40: * **System RAM:** **31 GiB DDR5** (+ 8 GiB Swap) 41: * **CUDA Environment:** CUDA 12.8 (Driver 570.172.08) 42: 43: --- 44: 45: ## 3. Architectural Decisions Record (ADR) 46: 47: | Decision ID | Topic | Decision | Rationale | 48: | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | 49: | **ADR-01** | **Implementation Strategy (Option 2 Selected)** | Build a **standalone Python + C++ prototyping pipeline** that exports multi-scalar diagnostic `.ply` files for CloudCompare first; defer native C++/CUDA integration into `preprocess_core` until validated. | Rapidly validates feature separability, $\ell_0$-cut pursuit regularization, and graph filtering thresholds via visual inspection in CloudCompare before committing to low-level C++/CUDA kernel refactoring. | 50: | **ADR-02** | **Unsupervised Superpoint Filtering Prior to Supervised SPT** | Replace immediate supervised Transformer training (DALES transfer learning, 4-class Lovász-Softmax) with **unsupervised/physical superpoint graph filtering** driven by CloudCompare-style geometric and enclosure descriptors. | Because trusted semantic labels do not exist across the 38 S3 clouds, supervised neural network fine-tuning cannot be executed directly. However, SPT's non-parametric $\ell_0$-cut pursuit + superpoint graph rules require zero labels and can later generate pseudo-labels if supervised training is desired. | 51: | **ADR-03** | **Global Subsampling & Global Features Before Spatial Tiling** | Reverse Step 1 of the initial draft: run **global $3\text{ cm}–4\text{ cm}$ subsampling**, **global normal orientation (WNNC)**, and **global upward enclosure** on the full cloud *before* any spatial tiling. | Slicing a cave into $40\text{ m} \times 40\text{ m}$ tiles before computing ambient occlusion or upward raycasting detaches high cavern ceilings from floors near tile boundaries, creating false "open-sky" artifacts inside deep chambers. | 52: | **ADR-04** | **Mandatory `float64` Centroid Subtraction** | Always compute and subtract the cloud centroid in `float64` (`pos_f64 - mean_f64`) before casting coordinates to `float32`. | Scans in projected national grids (e.g., Swiss LV95 $X \approx 2.53 \times 10^6\text{ m}$ in `BaumeDeLongeaigue.ply`) suffer a **$0.25\text{ m}$ `float32` quantization step (ULP)**, which destroys $3\text{ cm}$ voxelization and local covariance eigenvalues if cast prior to centering. | 53: | **ADR-05** | **Trajectory-Free Normal Orientation via WNNC** | Use **Winding Number Normal Consistency (WNNC)** ([src/wnnc](file:///home/projval/Documents/cgal/src/wnnc)) instead of sensor-trajectory orientation. | None of the 38 S3 clouds have trajectory files, and 35 of 38 lack `Gps_Time`. WNNC globally orients normals consistently inward/outward without trajectories. | 54: | **ADR-06** | **Purely Geometric + Enclosure Feature Bank (Drop `Intensity` & `RGB`)** | Exclude `scalar_Intensity`, `RGB`, and raw elevation $z$ from the classification logic; rely exclusively on translation-invariant multi-scale geometry and 3D roof enclosure. | 12 of 38 S3 clouds lack `Intensity`, and some clouds (`rupt.ply`) contain synthetic grayscale duplicated across `R=G=B`. Pure geometry + enclosure works identically on minimal `(x, y, z)` clouds (`lapa_da_onça`, `lapa_dos_troncos`, `lapinha`). | 55: 56: --- 57: 58: ## 4. End-to-End Pipeline Architecture (Option 2) 59: 60: ```mermaid 61: flowchart TD 62: A["S3 / Local Input Cloud (.ply)"] --> B["Stage 1: Float64 Centering &\nGlobal 3-4cm Grid Subsampling"] 63: B --> C["Stage 2: Global Normal Orientation\n(CUDA WNNC / Coherent Inward Normals)"] 64: C --> D["Stage 3: Multi-Scale P0 Feature Extraction\n(Fine r=0.15m, Coarse r=0.50m + Upward Cone Occlusion)"] 65: D --> E["Stage 4: l0-Cut Pursuit Partition\n(P0 Voxels -> P1 Fine Superpoints -> P2 Coarse Superpoints)"] 66: E --> F["Stage 5: Superpoint Graph Scoring\n& Geodesic / Roof-Enclosure Filtering"] 67: F --> G["Stage 6A: Diagnostic Multi-Scalar .ply\n(Inspectable in CloudCompare)"] 68: F --> H["Stage 6B: Cleaned Cavern .ply\n(Ready for PoissonRecon & Skeletonization)"] 69: ``` 70: 71: ### Stage 1: Ingestion, `float64` Coordinate Centering & Global $P_0$ Subsampling 72: 1. Parse ASCII or binary little-endian `.ply` from S3 (`https://ufmg-vale-esp-artefatos.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/point-clouds/`) or local `input/`. 73: 2. Store the original `float64` centroid $\boldsymbol{\mu} = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N \mathbf{p}_i$ in metadata so exported clouds can be restored to their original coordinate system. 74: 3. Translate points: $\tilde{\mathbf{p}}_i = \text{float32}(\mathbf{p}_i - \boldsymbol{\mu})$. 75: 4. Apply a $P_0$ voxel grid subsample at **$d_0 = 0.03\text{ m}$ to $0.04\text{ m}$** (using either the repository's [`CudaDecimator`](file:///home/projval/Documents/cgal/src/preprocess/src/cuda_decimator.cu) or fast 64-bit spatial voxel hashing in Python/C++). For a 10M-point S3 cloud, this produces **$1.5\text{M}–3.5\text{M}$ evenly spaced points**, homogenizing TLS/SLAM density gradients and bounding RAM usage well within 31 GB. 76: 77: ### Stage 2: Global Normal Orientation (WNNC) 78: 1. If the input cloud lacks reliable oriented normals, run the repository's CUDA-accelerated **WNNC** solver ([src/wnnc](file:///home/projval/Documents/cgal/src/wnnc)) on the subsampled cloud. 79: 2. Enforce consistent **inward-pointing cavern convention** (or outward convention verified via signed winding number gradient): 80: * **Cavern Ceiling:** normal points **downward** ($n_z < -0.25$). 81: * **Cavern Floor & Exterior Ground:** normal points **upward** ($n_z > +0.25$). 82: * **Cavern Walls & Tree Trunks:** normal is horizontal ($|n_z| \approx 0$). 83: 84: ### Stage 3: Multi-Scale CloudCompare & SPT Feature Bank ($P_0$) 85: For each subsampled point $p_i$, compute the local $3 \times 3$ covariance matrix over spherical neighborhoods at **two spatial scales** ($r_{\text{fine}} = 0.15\text{ m}$ to capture leaves/twigs, and $r_{\text{coarse}} = 0.50\text{ m}$ to capture rock sheets vs. bush canopies), yielding ordered eigenvalues $\lambda_1 \ge \lambda_2 \ge \lambda_3 \ge 0$ and eigenvectors $\mathbf{v}_1, \mathbf{v}_2, \mathbf{v}_3$: 86: 87: #### A. Local Eigen-Descriptors & Normal Statistics (Computed at $r_{\text{fine}}$ and $r_{\text{coarse}}$) 88: * **Verticality:** 89: $$V = 1 - |n_z| \in [0, 1]$$ 90: * **Horizontality & Signed Horizontality:** 91: $$H = |n_z| \in [0, 1], \quad H_{\text{signed}} = n_z \in [-1, 1]$$ 92: *(Crucial cue: $n_z < -0.25$ uniquely identifies overhanging bedrock and cavern ceilings, which never occur on exterior ground).* 93: * **Rugosity / Surface Variation (CloudCompare Curvature):** 94: $$\kappa = \frac{\lambda_3}{\lambda_1 + \lambda_2 + \lambda_3} \in \left[0, \frac{1}{3}\right]$$ 95: *(Cavern rock sheets have $\kappa_{\text{coarse}} < 0.06$; foliage and bushes approach isotropic 3D scattering $\kappa \in [0.15, 0.33]$).* 96: * **Planarity, Linearity, and Scattering (Sphericity):** 97: $$P = \frac{\lambda_2 - \lambda_3}{\lambda_1}, \quad L = \frac{\lambda_1 - \lambda_2}{\lambda_1}, \quad S = \frac{\lambda_3}{\lambda_1}$$ 98: * **Normal Dispersion / Roughness Entropy:** 99: $$D_{\mathbf{n}} = 1 - \left\| \frac{1}{|\mathcal{N}_r(i)|} \sum_{j \in \mathcal{N}_r(i)} \mathbf{n}_j \right\|_2 \in [0, 1]$$ 100: *(Even fractured or scalloped cave walls maintain coherent normal orientations at $r = 0.20\text{ m}$ ($D_{\mathbf{n}} < 0.18$), whereas foliage exhibits chaotic normals ($D_{\mathbf{n}} > 0.45$)).* 101: 102: #### B. Global 3D Enclosure Descriptors (Solving Speleothem vs. Vegetation Ambiguity) 103: Because fragile speleothems (stalactites, coralloids, breakdown rubble) inside a cave can locally mimic the high `Scattering` and `Rugosity` of tree branches, we compute two global enclosure scalars on the full cloud using a coarse spatial hash / octree ($10\text{ cm}–15\text{ cm}$ cells): 104: 1. **Upward Cone Occlusion Ratio ($O_{\text{up}} \in [0, 1]$):** 105: * Cast $K = 32$ rays from each point $p_i$ within an upward cone of $\pm 50^\circ$ around $+Z$ (starting at offset $r_{\min} = 0.50\text{ m}$ to avoid self-occlusion by a tree's own twig, up to $r_{\max} = 60\text{ m}$). 106: * Record the fraction of rays that intersect an overhanging rock surface (weighted higher if the hit surface has a downward-pointing normal $n_z < 0$ or low normal dispersion). 107: * **Inside Cavern Conduits:** $O_{\text{up}} \in [0.80, 1.00]$ (solid bedrock ceiling overhead). 108: * **Exterior Terrain & Vegetation Outside Drip Line:** $O_{\text{up}} \in [0.00, 0.30]$ (open sky overhead). 109: 2. **Upper-Hemisphere Sky-View Factor / Ambient Occlusion (`PCV`):** 110: * Re-use `scalar_Illuminance_(PCV)` where already present in Cohort A, or compute fast hemispherical visibility over 64 directions. 111: 112: ### Stage 4: Hierarchical $\ell_0$-Cut Pursuit Superpoint Partitioning ($P_0 \to P_1 \to P_2$) 113: Instead of thresholding noisy point features individually: 114: 1. Build the $k$-NN spatial adjacency graph ($k = 10$) on the $P_0$ voxels. 115: 2. Construct the **partition feature vector** $\mathbf{f}_i \in \mathbb{R}^d$ by concatenating normalized geometric and enclosure features: 116: $$\mathbf{f}_i = \left[ P_{\text{fine}},\, S_{\text{fine}},\, L_{\text{fine}},\, \kappa_{\text{coarse}},\, V,\, H_{\text{signed}},\, D_{\mathbf{n}},\, w_{\text{occ}} \cdot O_{\text{up}} \right]$$ 117: *(Including $O_{\text{up}}$ directly in the cut-pursuit objective forces a sharp superpoint boundary right along the cave entrance drip line).* 118: 3. Run parallel **$\ell_0$-cut pursuit** (`grid_graph` / `cp_d0_dist`) with: 119: * `pcp_regularization = [0.04, 0.15]` 120: * `pcp_spatial_weight = [0.05, 0.02]` 121: * `pcp_cutoff = [10, 30]` 122: This compresses millions of $P_0$ points into **$5,000–25,000$ geometrically homogeneous $P_1$ superpoints** and **$500–3,000$ regional $P_2$ superpoints**. 123: 124: ### Stage 5: Superpoint Graph Scoring & Topological Geodesic Filtering 125: For each $P_1$ superpoint $\mathcal{S}_k$, aggregate the robust median/mean of its constituent $P_0$ features and evaluate a two-step graph filter: 126: 127: 1. **Superpoint Unary Prior Score:** 128: * **High-Confidence Cavern Seeds ($\mathcal{C}_{\text{seed}}$):** 129: * Overhanging/ceiling superpoints ($H_{\text{signed}} < -0.25$ and $D_{\mathbf{n}} < 0.30$), **OR** 130: * Roof-enclosed superpoints ($O_{\text{up}} > 0.80$ and $D_{\mathbf{n}} < 0.35$). 131: * **High-Confidence Vegetation / Clutter Seeds ($\mathcal{V}_{\text{seed}}$):** 132: * Unenclosed high-entropy superpoints ($O_{\text{up}} < 0.40$ AND $[\kappa_{\text{fine}} > 0.12 \text{ OR } S_{\text{fine}} > 0.35 \text{ OR } D_{\mathbf{n}} > 0.40]$). 133: * **High-Confidence Exterior Terrain Seeds ($\mathcal{T}_{\text{seed}}$):** 134: * Unenclosed upward-facing planar surfaces outside the drip line ($O_{\text{up}} < 0.15$, $H_{\text{signed}} > +0.50$, and geodesic distance from any overhanging ceiling superpoint $> 5\text{ m}$). 135: 136: 2. **Topological Graph Propagation & Speleothem Protection:** 137: * **Internal Speleothem Rule:** Any high-rugosity/high-scattering cluster that is (a) at geodesic graph distance $> 15\text{ m}$ from the exterior boundary **AND** (b) covered by a solid roof ($O_{\text{up}} > 0.80$) is locked as **`Cavern`**. 138: * **Skylight / Collapsed Doline Exception:** If a high-rugosity cluster lies laterally inside a cave system but has **open sky directly above it** ($O_{\text{up}} < 0.35$, e.g., trees growing on the floor of a skylight/claraboia), it remains classified as **`Vegetation (Remove)`**. 139: * **Tree Trunk & Branch Stripping:** High-linearity/vertical superpoints outside the drip line ($O_{\text{up}} < 0.45$) that are adjacent in the $P_1$ graph to $\mathcal{V}_{\text{seed}}$ canopy superpoints are absorbed into **`Vegetation (Remove)`** via graph label propagation / min-cut. 140: 141: ### Stage 6: Diagnostic CloudCompare Export & Downstream Reconstruction 142: The standalone pipeline outputs two `.ply` files per cave (restored to original `float64` coordinates): 143: 1. **`_diagnostic.ply` (for CloudCompare inspection):** 144: Contains all $P_0$ points with scalar fields: 145: * `scalar_verticality` 146: * `scalar_signed_horizontality` 147: * `scalar_rugosity_fine` 148: * `scalar_rugosity_coarse` 149: * `scalar_planarity` 150: * `scalar_scattering` 151: * `scalar_normal_dispersion` 152: * `scalar_upward_occlusion` 153: * `scalar_superpoint_p1` 154: * `scalar_cavern_score` (`[0.0, 1.0]`) 155: * `scalar_predicted_class` (`0 = Cavern`, `1 = Vegetation`, `2 = Exterior Terrain / Clutter`) 156: 2. **`_cleaned.ply`:** 157: Contains only the retained `Cavern` points ($P_0$ or full-resolution points mapped back via nearest $P_0$ voxel), ready to pass directly into `./build/pipeline` (`WNNC` $\to$ `PoissonRecon` $\to$ `SurfaceTrimmer` $\to$ `skeletonization`). 158: 159: --- 160: 161: ## 5. Future Extension: Weakly-Supervised SPT / Classifier Training 162: 163: Once the unsupervised superpoint pipeline has been validated on 5–10 representative S3 caves in CloudCompare: 164: 1. Any subtle entrance transition errors can be corrected in minutes in CloudCompare by flipping the label of entire **$P_1 / P_2$ superpoints** rather than individual points. 165: 2. Those verified superpoint labels can then be used to train either: 166: * A fast **LightGBM / CatBoost / MLP classifier** over the $[P_1 \oplus P_2]$ multi-scale superpoint graph features (trains in $< 10\text{ seconds}$ on CPU/GPU), or 167: * The full **Superpoint Transformer (SPT)** self-attention head on the cached NAG files (`datamodule.max_num_nodes = 20000`, `precision = 16-mixed` to fit within the 6 GB RTX 4050 VRAM budget), grouped strictly by **cave system** (`hoelloch_*`, `archamps_*`, `encanaux_*`, `S11D_*`) during cross-validation. 168: 169: --- 170: 171: ## 6. Empirical Benchmarks & Massive-Scale Optimizations (Up to 311.7M Points) 172: 173: The standalone pipeline is implemented in [spt_filter.py](file:///home/projval/Documents/cgal/spt_filter.py) backed by C++20 OpenMP/Eigen3/WNNC kernels in [src/spt_filter/spt_kernels.cpp](file:///home/projval/Documents/cgal/src/spt_filter/spt_kernels.cpp) (`build/libspt_kernels.so`). 174: 175: ### Key Algorithmic & Scaling Refinements 176: 1. **Always-On Global WNNC Normal Estimation & Physical Raycast Verification:** 177: - Pre-existing `.ply` normals in Cohort A (`BaumeDeLongeaigue.ply`, `diaclase.ply`) are frequently unoriented or outward-pointing, which previously inverted `signed_horizontality` ($n_z$) and scrambled Floor vs. Ceiling separation. 178: - Stage 2A now unconditionally executes the **Winding Number Normal Consistency (WNNC)** solver ([`spt_compute_wnnc_normals`](file:///home/projval/Documents/cgal/src/spt_filter/spt_kernels.cpp#L1133-L1290)) over a 60,000-point carrier cloud ($40\text{ iterations}$, $O(N \log N)$ Barnes-Hut octree treecode) and propagates inward-oriented normals to all $P_0$ voxels. 179: - Stage 2B blends the global WNNC orientation with local PCA eigenvectors proportionally to surface planarity while computing sign-invariant structure tensor dispersion ($D_{\mathbf{n}}$) on unsmoothed local PCA directions (expanding sparse neighborhood searches up to $3r$ so low-density cave vaults never trigger high-entropy fallbacks). 180: - Stage 3 ([`spt_compute_enclosure`](file:///home/projval/Documents/cgal/src/spt_filter/spt_kernels.cpp#L606-L790)) verifies physical normal polarity along $\pm Z$ using **rock-coherent occlusion**: points with a coherent rock ceiling above ($O_{\text{roof}} > O_{\text{down,rock}} + 0.12$) are enforced to point upward ($n_z > 0$, **Floor**), while points with a rock floor below and no rock ceiling above ($O_{\text{down,rock}} > O_{\text{roof}} + 0.12$) are enforced to point downward ($n_z < 0$, **Ceiling**)—even when tall trees grow on the hillside above the cave. 181: 2. **Explicit Floor / Wall / Ceiling Structural Zone Separation (`scalar_cave_zone`):** 182: - Stage 4 incorporates strongly weighted `signed_horizontality` ($1.2 \times n_z$) and vertical occlusion differential ($0.8 \times (O_{\text{roof}} - O_{\text{down}})$) into the $\ell_0$-cut pursuit feature vector so $P_1$ superpoints never merge floors, walls, and ceilings across cave conduits. 183: - Stage 5 classifies every Cavern superpoint into explicit structural zones exported to `scalar_cave_zone`: `0 = Floor` ($n_z \ge +0.35$), `1 = Wall` ($|n_z| < 0.35$), `2 = Ceiling` ($n_z \le -0.35$), alongside `3 = Vegetation` and `4 = Exterior Ground`. 184: 3. **2D-Manifold-Gated Cone Raycasting (`roof_occlusion` vs. `upward_occlusion`):** 185: - In tropical forest caves (`Lp_JL.ply`, `point-clouds_S11A_0257.ply`, `Lp_Boi.ply`), 15–25m tall trees outside and above the entrance cause lower canopy branches and exterior ground to experience high raw upward ray hits ($O_{\text{up}} \in [0.56, 0.97]$). 186: - Weighting occupancy cells by coarse-scale 2D rock coherence ($P_{\text{coarse}} > 0.32, D_{\mathbf{n},\text{coarse}} < 0.35, \kappa_{\text{coarse}} < 0.12, S_{\text{coarse}} < 0.25$) ensures porous 3D leaf canopies contribute `0.000–0.004` to `roof_occlusion`, while true bedrock ceilings yield high `roof_occlusion`. 187: 4. **Positive-Evidence Canopy Detection & Topological Connected-Component Filtering (0% False Positives on Interior Caves):** 188: - Replaced catch-all negative scoring with positive-evidence multi-scale 3D foliage criteria (requiring simultaneous fine-scale and coarse-scale volumetric scattering, rugosity, and normal dispersion under open sky $O_{\text{roof}} < 0.15$). 189: - Scaled feature radii proportionally to voxel size ($r_{\text{fine,eff}} = \max(r_{\text{fine}}, 3.75\,d_0)$, $r_{\text{coarse,eff}} = \max(r_{\text{coarse}}, 10.0\,d_0)$) to prevent discrete voxel-lattice staircasing on $8\text{ cm}–12\text{ cm}$ grids. 190: - Implemented **Step 5 Topological Superpoint Graph Connected-Component Filtering**: candidate exterior vegetation superpoints are clustered in 3D space and validated only if the connected component has macroscopic size ($\ge 500$ $P_0$ voxels, $\ge 300$ canopy voxels) **and** extends into open exterior space ($> 4.5\text{ m}$ from any enclosed cave vault seed). Rough wall pockets or stalactite clusters inside pure interior caves (`rupt`, `BaumeDeLongeaigue`, `diaclase`, `interior_lapinha`) stay within $\le 4.07\text{ m}$ of the cave vault and are 100% retained as `Cavern`. 191: 5. **Out-of-Core Chunked Streaming for 100M–300M+ Point Clouds:** 192: - `stream_subsample_ply` and `stream_export_cleaned_ply` stream 15M-vertex chunks from disk and map $P_0$ predictions and WNNC-oriented normals back to full resolution via `spt_map_points_to_p0`, keeping peak memory under **3.5 GB RAM**. 193: 194: ### Benchmark Summary Across 7 Diverse Caves + 3D CutMix Stress Test 195: 196: | Cave Scan | Input Points ($N_{\text{orig}}$) | $P_0$ Voxels ($N_{P_0}$) | $P_1 \to P_2$ Superpoints | Cavern Retained ($P_0$ / Full-Res) | Vegetation + Ext. Ground Removed ($P_0$) | Structural Cave Zones ($P_0$: Floor / Wall / Ceiling) | Pipeline Runtime | 197: | :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | :--- | ---: | 198: | `rupt.ply` *(Interior)* | 346,954 | 346,403 ($4\text{ cm}$) | $3,302 \to 323$ | **100.00%** (346,954 pts) | **0 (0.00%)** | 46.0% / 20.3% / 33.6% | **8.51s** | 199: | `BaumeDeLongeaigue.ply` *(Interior)* | 373,198 | 371,773 ($4\text{ cm}$) | $5,231 \to 424$ | **100.00%** (373,198 pts) | **0 (0.00%)** | 37.2% / 21.8% / 41.0% | **7.59s** | 200: | `diaclase.ply` *(Interior Fissure)* | 171,931 | 140,717 ($4\text{ cm}$) | $2,932 \to 209$ | **100.00%** (171,931 pts) | **0 (0.00%)** | 33.5% / 27.2% / 39.3% | **11.02s** |

I have launched the updated SPT filter benchmark suite across the interior test caves (`rupt.ply`, `BaumeDeLongeaigue.ply`, `diaclase.ply`, `interior_lapinha.ply`), `point-clouds_S11A_0257.ply`, and `Lp_JL.ply` (`--voxel-size 0.08`) to verify the Part 1–3 fixes.
